title: Learning Quantum Gibbs States Locally and Efficiently
authors: Chi-Fang Chen (UC Berkeley, USA), Anurag Anshu (Harvard University, USA), Quynh T. Nguyen (Harvard University, USA)
abstract: Learning the Hamiltonian underlying a quantum many-body system in thermal equilibrium is a fundamental task in quantum learning theory and experimental sciences. To learn the Gibbs state of local Hamiltonians at any constant inverse temperature, the state-of-the-art provable algorithms fall short of the optimal sample and computational complexity, in sharp contrast with the locality and simplicity in the classical cases. In this work, we present a learning algorithm that learns each local term of a n-qubit Hamiltonian on any bounded-degree graph to a constant additive error with the optimal sample complexity O(\log n). The protocol uses parallelizable local quantum measurements that act within bounded neighborhoods of the graph and near-linear-time classical post-processing. We also give a learning algorithm for lattice Hamiltonians with near-optimal scaling on the learning precision and the inverse temperature. At the heart of our algorithm is the interplay between locality, the Kubo-Martin-Schwinger condition, and the operator Fourier transform at arbitrary temperatures.
